reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents the Coinbase One Card as an ordinary card product with a stated bitcoin-back reward of up to 4%, along with terms, eligibility, and approval conditions. The described material does not show a deceptive mechanism, a request for credentials or payment outside the card product, or a guaranteed return or investment solicitation.

citations.quote: The Coinbase One Card is here. Earn up to 4% bitcoin back on every purchase.
Terms apply. Subject to eligibility and approval. Bitcoin back rewards rates are based on the cardholder’s assets held on Coinbase. We’ll share more when the Card becomes available.

opening.argument: The central message links a concrete viewer action to acquiring bitcoin: viewers are told to spend dollars and make bitcoin, while the offer promises up to 4% bitcoin back on every purchase. That is a participation pathway, not merely neutral discussion. The description also directs viewers to Coinbase, so the reward claim and the route toward the provider appear together as a solicitation for card use and platform participation.

citations.quote: The Coinbase One Card is here. Earn up to 4% bitcoin back on every purchase.
To own a piece of the future visit Coinbase

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this an ordinary card does not resolve the persuasive structure. The material foregrounds a bitcoin reward and directs viewers toward Coinbase, while the qualifications are secondary conditions. Saying that eligibility and approval apply does not establish that the advertised reward is straightforward, valuable, or available to the typical viewer. The combination still asks viewers to participate in a crypto-linked offer.

citations.quote: The Coinbase One Card is here. Earn up to 4% bitcoin back on every purchase.
Subject to eligibility and approval.
To own a piece of the future visit Coinbase

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted linkage shows only a purchase-linked card reward, not a deceptive claim or an unearned asset acquisition. The offer expressly says that eligibility and approval apply, and that reward rates depend on assets held on Coinbase. Those conditions contradict the suggestion that the reward is presented as universally available or effortless.

citations.quote: Terms apply. Subject to eligibility and approval.
Bitcoin back rewards rates are based on the cardholder’s assets held on Coinbase.

opening.argument: Several risk signals are concentrated in a short promotion: crypto is presented as something viewers can earn from routine spending, with a headline rate of up to 4%, and the audience is sent to an external Coinbase destination. The message also uses the expansive language of turning old money into new money, which can make the reward sound like an easy transformation rather than a limited, conditional benefit. Taken together, the crypto terminology, prominent rate, and action link warrant treating the offer as potentially deceptive.

citations.quote: Earn up to 4% bitcoin back on every purchase.
turning old money into new money, again and again.
http://coinbase.com/creditcard

rebuttal.rebuttal: The presence of crypto language and an external web address is not proof of ordinary commerce. What matters is the framing: the most memorable claim is an apparently easy bitcoin return attached to every purchase. The later conditions do not explain the actual rate, its practical value, or whether the average viewer qualifies. The risk signals therefore remain material rather than harmless background details.

citations.quote: Earn up to 4% bitcoin back on every purchase.
We’ll share more when the Card becomes available.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The argument turns ordinary qualifiers into suspicion without evidence of deception. The material does not promise a fixed return: it says up to 4%, makes eligibility and approval applicable, ties rates to assets held on Coinbase, and says more details will come later. Those statements limit the offer rather than conceal its conditional nature.

citations.quote: Terms apply. Subject to eligibility and approval.
Bitcoin back rewards rates are based on the cardholder’s assets held on Coinbase.
We’ll share more when the Card becomes available.

opening.argument: Although the material can be described as an announcement about a card, its function is plainly promotional: it names the product, highlights a bitcoin reward, tells viewers to visit Coinbase, and asks them to subscribe and follow the company. The line about owning a piece of the future adds aspirational pressure around participation. This is therefore not detached education about crypto; it steers viewers toward a branded purchase-linked opportunity whose reward is the main attraction.

citations.quote: Coinbase One Card
To own a piece of the future visit Coinbase
✅ Subscribe to our channel here:
► Follow us on Twitter:

rebuttal.rebuttal: The product framing is precisely why the content deserves scrutiny: it uses branded promotion and aspirational language to direct participation, not simply to explain how cards work. The disclaimer that the content is informational does not erase the explicit invitation to visit Coinbase or the prominent reward claim. A promotional disclaimer cannot by itself make the solicitation non-deceptive.

citations.quote: Nothing discussed in this video is intended to be investment advice.
To own a piece of the future visit Coinbase
Earn up to 4% bitcoin back on every purchase.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion alone is not a scam. The content identifies the product and supplies ordinary promotional conditions rather than hiding them: eligibility and approval apply, reward rates depend on Coinbase-held assets, and availability is not yet fully described. The investment disclaimer further makes clear that the material is not a recommendation to buy, sell, or hold a financial product.
